diptych-of-federico-da-montefeltro-and-battista-sforza

A duke and his wife face each other in profile, painted as two panels that fold like a book, with a wide landscape behind them. Piero della Francesca painted it in about 1470. Federico's nose looks odd because he lost his right eye and part of his nose in a tournament, so he always showed his left side.
monforte-altarpiece
The three kings kneel in a ruined stable to honor the baby Jesus, in a large, crowded panel. Hugo van der Goes painted it in about 1470, and the faces look like real people from the town.
portrait-of-a-girl
A young woman in profile wears pearls and a golden net in her hair, with a pale sky behind her. Piero del Pollaiuolo painted it in about 1470, and you can see every jewel.
portrait-of-a-young-girl
A girl in a plain dark dress and a cap looks out shyly, with a hint of a smile. Petrus Christus painted it in about 1470, and she may be the daughter of a rich family.
portrait-of-federico-da-montefeltro-with-his-son-guidob

A duke sits in full armor, reading a book, while his young son stands beside him holding a scepter. It is attributed to either Justus of Ghent or Pedro Berruguete, around 1470, and Federico was a famous soldier who loved books.
portrait-of-maria-portinari

A young woman in a tall black hat and a red gown with a gold necklace looks calmly out at you. Hans Memling painted Maria Portinari in about 1470, and she was the wife of a rich banker from Florence living in Bruges.
saint-george-and-the-dragon-uccello

A knight on a white horse stabs a dragon, while a princess leads the monster away on a string like a pet. Paolo Uccello painted it in the 1470s, and the sky, with a swirly storm cloud, adds to the drama.
scenes-from-the-passion-of-christ

Dozens of tiny scenes tell the story of Jesus's last days, in a busy city with towers and gates. Hans Memling painted this in about 1470, and the artist put the whole story in a single picture, so you can follow it like a comic strip.
st-john-altarpiece

Mary and the baby Jesus sit in the center, with saints and angels beside them and scenes from John the Baptist and John the Evangelist on the side panels. Hans Memling painted it in about 1470 for a hospital in Bruges.
the-baptism-of-christ

John the Baptist pours water on Jesus in a river while angels kneel at the bank. Andrea del Verrocchio painted most of it, but a young Leonardo da Vinci painted the angel on the left and part of the landscape around 1470, and people say Verrocchio was amazed at how good he was.
the-hunt-in-the-forest

Hunters on horses and on foot, with dogs, chase deer through a dark forest in this picture where all the trees line up toward a far-off point. Paolo Uccello painted it in about 1470, and he loved perspective so much that he made a game of it.
tobias-and-the-angel

A boy walks beside an angel, holding a little fish and the angel's hand, with a small dog trotting along. It comes from the workshop of Andrea del Verrocchio in the 1470s, and the boy and angel are on a journey from the Bible.
vienna-diptych

Adam and Eve stand beside a tree with a serpent on one panel, and on the other panel the sad story of Christ's death is shown in gray. Hugo van der Goes painted it in about 1470, to show how the sin of the first people led to Christ's sacrifice.
portrait-of-galeazzo-maria-sforza
A young duke in rich clothes looks sideways in profile, with a dark background. Piero del Pollaiuolo painted Galeazzo Maria Sforza in 1471, and he was the ruler of Milan.
annunciation

The angel Gabriel kneels in a garden to tell Mary she will have a baby, while she sits at her desk. Leonardo da Vinci painted this when he was about 20, in 1472, and the angel's wings are modeled on a real bird's.
madonna-and-child-with-saints-angels-and-federico-da-mo

Mary sits on a throne under a giant shell, with saints and angels around her and a duke in armor kneeling on one side. Piero della Francesca painted it in 1472, and an ostrich egg hangs from the shell to tell you how perfect she is.
tavola-strozzi

A fleet of ships comes into the harbor of Naples while a crowd cheers from the shore. Francesco Rosselli is credited with this panel from about 1472, and it is one of the earliest views of a city from the sea.
virgin-and-child

Mary holds the baby Jesus in front of a golden cloth, and a ripe apple and garland of fruit hang above them. Carlo Crivelli painted it in 1472, in his jeweled style, with every curl and gem carefully drawn.
madonna-of-the-rose-bower

Mary sits in a garden full of roses with the baby Jesus, while angels hold a crown above her head. Martin Schongauer painted it in 1473 for a church in Colmar, and the golden background makes it glow.
man-with-a-roman-coin

A man in black holds up a coin from ancient Rome, with a palm tree and a landscape behind him. Hans Memling painted him in about 1473, and the coin shows the emperor Nero. It is thought to be Bernardo Bembo, a Venetian diplomat.
saint-jerome-in-his-study
A scholar saint reads in a huge room under Gothic arches, with a peacock, a lion and a cat in the background. Antonello da Messina painted it in 1474, and the room is full of beautiful tiny details.
adoration-of-the-magi-botticelli

The three kings kneel before the baby Jesus in this crowded picture, and in the crowd Botticelli painted members of the Medici family, and himself, staring out at us in a yellow cloak. He painted it in about 1475.
calvary
Christ hangs on the cross between two other crosses under a calm blue sky, with Mary and John grieving. Antonello da Messina painted it in about 1475, with a view of the peaceful countryside.
contarini-madonna
Mary holds the baby Jesus in front of a green cloth, with a landscape of hills and clouds behind them. Giovanni Bellini painted it around 1475, and he was the best painter in Venice.
madonna-of-the-carnation

Mary holds out a red carnation to the baby Jesus, who reaches for it with his chubby hand. Leonardo da Vinci painted it in about 1475 when he was in his twenties, with a pretty landscape through the two windows behind.
martyrdom-of-saint-sebastian

Saint Sebastian is tied to a tree and shot with arrows by six archers, each in a different, active pose. Antonio and Piero del Pollaiuolo painted this in 1475, and they studied how muscles work to get the poses right.
portinari-triptych

Shepherds and angels gather around the newborn Jesus in the middle panel, while the donors kneel with their saints on the sides. Hugo van der Goes painted it in about 1475, and it was shipped to Florence where it amazed artists.
portrait-of-a-lady-pollaiuolo
A young woman in profile wears a gold and pearl net on her hair, with a tall forehead and graceful neck. Antonio del Pollaiuolo painted her in about 1475.
portrait-of-a-man
A young man in a dark cap looks at you with a faint smile and bright eyes. Antonello da Messina painted it in about 1475, and the smile makes it feel as if he is about to speak.
portrait-of-a-man-called-condottiere

A scarred man with a bold stare and a bristling haircut looks right at you. Antonello da Messina painted it in about 1475, and the name Condottiere means a leader of mercenary soldiers, but nobody knows who he really was.
the-burning-bush

Moses kneels near a bush that is on fire, but not burning up, while the Virgin Mary and the child sit within it. Nicolas Froment painted this triptych in about 1475, and the bush is a sign of how God appeared to Moses.
tobias-and-the-angel-lippi
A boy walks along with an angel while carrying a fish, with a little dog trotting beside them. Filippino Lippi painted it in about 1475, and the angel's cloak flows in the breeze.
virgin-annunciate

Mary raises one hand and holds her cloak with the other, looking up as if she has just been told she will have a baby. Antonello da Messina painted this in about 1475, and the angel isn't shown, so you feel the surprise as if you were the angel.
ginevra-de-benci

A pale young woman with curly hair stands before a juniper bush, and her gaze is cool and distant. Leonardo da Vinci painted her portrait in about 1476, when she was about 17. This is the only painting by Leonardo in the Americas.
madonna-di-senigallia

Mary and the baby Jesus stand in a plain, bright room, and two angels hold up small, calm faces beside them. Piero della Francesca painted it in about 1476, and the light pours in from the window in the wall.
christ-at-the-column-messina

Christ stands with a rope around his neck and a crown of thorns, and a single tear runs down his cheek. Antonello da Messina painted it in 1477, and the sad, gentle face is very powerful for such a small picture.
madonna-and-child-with-a-pomegranate
Mary holds the baby Jesus, who has a pomegranate in his little hand, in front of a window with a landscape. Lorenzo di Credi painted it in about 1477, and he was a friend of Leonardo da Vinci.
saint-sebastian

Saint Sebastian, pierced with arrows, is tied to a column in a town square, and the street behind him goes on and on. Antonello da Messina painted it in about 1478, and the perspective of the street is wonderfully exact.
transfiguration-of-christ

Christ glows with white light on a mountain while Moses and Elijah stand beside him, and his friends cower below. Giovanni Bellini painted it in about 1478, and the green hills and quiet sky in the back are as beautiful as anything in his career.
trinity-altarpiece

A king and his sons kneel in their prayers to the saints, in these panels that were made for Scotland. Hugo van der Goes painted them in about 1478, and they are one of the rare great Flemish paintings still kept in Scotland.
santa-maria-in-porto-altarpiece
Mary sits on a throne with the baby Jesus while saints stand to both sides of her. Ercole de' Roberti painted this altarpiece in 1479 for a church in Ravenna.
adoration-of-the-shepherds-goes

The shepherds hurry in to see the baby Jesus, and a curtain is pulled back to reveal the scene. Hugo van der Goes painted it in about 1480, and the shepherds' faces are painted with a great deal of feeling.
advent-and-triumph-of-christ
Dozens of tiny scenes of Jesus's life run through a wide landscape, with towns, roads and trees across the picture. Hans Memling painted this in about 1480, and it is like a big storybook page.
annunciation-memling
The angel Gabriel kneels in front of Mary in a bright room with a bed and a pitcher of lilies. Hans Memling painted it in about 1480, and the little details of the room are charming.
benois-madonna

Mary smiles at her baby, who tries to catch a flower in her hand, in front of a bright window. Leonardo da Vinci painted this when he was about 28, around 1480, and it is one of the sweetest of all Madonnas.
john-the-baptist-in-the-wilderness

John the Baptist sits in a green, peaceful landscape with a lamb, resting his head on his hand as if he were daydreaming. Geertgen tot Sint Jans painted it in about 1480, and the animals and plants are painted with great love.
madonna-and-child-crivelli
Mary holds the baby Jesus, who has an apple, while garlands of fruit hang above them. Carlo Crivelli painted it in about 1480, and he liked to paint real, shiny objects like fruit and flies.
man-of-sorrows
Christ sits on his tomb with his hands crossed, looking weary and pained, and his wounds show. Geertgen tot Sint Jans painted it in about 1480, and he was a young Dutch painter who died at about 28.
mary-magdalen

Mary Magdalene looks out of the picture with a jar of ointment and long, rippling hair. Carlo Crivelli painted it in about 1480, and the jewelry and clothes are painted to look like real silk and gems.
portrait-of-giovanna-tornabuoni

A young woman in a beautiful dress stands in profile in front of a shelf with a book and a jewel. Domenico Ghirlandaio painted her in 1488. She died in childbirth soon after, and a poem on the wall says that art could capture her face but not her soul.
portrait-of-simonetta-vespucci

A woman with braided hair and a pearl necklace stands against a stormy sky, with a snake coiled on her arm. Piero di Cosimo painted her around 1480, after she died as a young woman, and Florence mourned her as a beauty. The painting shows her bare shoulder and chest.
primavera

Venus, the Three Graces, Mercury, Zephyr and Flora stand in an orange grove where hundreds of flowers cover the ground. Sandro Botticelli painted it in about 1480, and botanists have counted over 500 plants in it. It's one of the most famous paintings of the Renaissance.
saint-francis-in-the-desert

A friar in a brown robe stands outside his cave, looking up into the light with his arms open. Giovanni Bellini painted it in about 1480, and the landscape, with its rocky hills, donkey and tiny town, is as important as the saint.
saint-jerome-in-the-wilderness

A thin, haggard Saint Jerome kneels in a rocky place and beats his chest with a stone, while a lion lies at his feet. Leonardo da Vinci painted it in about 1480, but he never finished it, so you can still see the outline underneath.
the-adoration-of-the-magi

Three kings, in rich clothes of green, red and gold, kneel before the baby Jesus in front of a ruined stable. Geertgen tot Sint Jans painted it in about 1480, and the kings' faces are different from one another.
the-nativity

Angels sing and play lutes beside the baby Jesus, who lies on the ground on a corner of Mary's cloak. Piero della Francesca painted it in about 1480, and an ox and a donkey look on, and the donkey brays at the top of his voice.
triptych-of-adriaan-reins
Christ's body is held in a picture from the Bible, and saints and the man who paid for it, Adriaan Reins, look on. Hans Memling painted it in 1480 for a hospital in Bruges, where it still hangs.
young-man-holding-a-roundel

A young man in a red cap holds up a small round painting of a saint, as if showing it to us. Sandro Botticelli painted him in about 1480, and the little round picture was probably painted by an older artist.
descent-from-mount-sinai
Moses comes down from the mountain with the Ten Commandments, while the people below worship a golden calf. Cosimo Rosselli and his workshop painted this fresco in the Sistine Chapel in 1481.
galitzin-triptych
Christ hangs on a cross with Mary and John, and saints on the side panels. Pietro Perugino painted it in about 1481, with calm, sweet faces and wide, hazy landscapes.
idealized-portrait-of-a-lady-portrait-of-simonetta-vesp

A woman with long, golden braids turns her head to the side, wearing a gauzy gown. Sandro Botticelli painted this around 1482, and it may show Simonetta Vespucci, the most celebrated beauty in Florence, as a nymph.
pallas-and-the-centaur

The goddess Pallas Athena holds a centaur, half man and half horse, by his hair, and a branch of olive is wound around her gown. Sandro Botticelli painted it in about 1482, and it may show wisdom taming wild instincts.
testament-and-death-of-moses
Moses, an old man, gives his last speech to the people on one side, and on the other he is buried on a mountain. Luca Signorelli painted this fresco in the Sistine Chapel in about 1482.
agony-in-the-garden-perugino
Jesus kneels alone in a hushed garden at dawn while his disciples sleep and angels bring him a cup. Pietro Perugino painted it in about 1483, and the colors make it shine.
lamentation-of-christ

Christ lies on a slab, seen from his feet, with weeping mourners at his head. Andrea Mantegna painted this in about 1483, and the foreshortening, which is the way he's drawn from the feet, is so dramatic that people still talk about it.
madonna-of-the-magnificat
Mary writes the word Magnificat in a book while the baby Jesus holds a pomegranate, and angels crown her with a golden crown. Sandro Botticelli painted this big round picture in about 1483.
pieta-perugino
Mary holds Christ's body in her lap while John and other friends mourn around him. Pietro Perugino painted it in about 1483, and the soft light and gentle faces give it a quiet peace.
moreel-triptych

The Moreel family kneels in the side panels, with a saint standing behind each of them, and Saint Christopher carries the child in the middle. Hans Memling painted this in 1484, and the faces of the family look like real people.
adoration-of-the-magi-ghirlandai

The kings arrive with a large crowd of followers, kneeling to the baby Jesus in front of a ruined arch. Domenico Ghirlandaio painted it in 1485, and he included lots of things from daily life in Florence.
annunciation-with-saints-john-the-baptist-and-andrew
The angel Gabriel and Mary face each other in the center, with two saints standing at the sides. Filippino Lippi painted it in about 1485, and the saints seem to be looking at us.
bathsheba-at-her-bath-memling

A woman bathes in a quiet pool beside a palace, while a servant helps her dress, and a king looks on from far above. Hans Memling painted it in about 1485, and it shows the Bible story of King David and Bathsheba.
crucifixion-with-a-donor

Christ hangs on the cross against a dark sky, with a small man kneeling at the foot. Hieronymus Bosch painted it in about 1485, and the donor kneeling at the cross is shown much smaller than Mary and the saints.
madonna-of-jacob-floreins
Mary and the baby Jesus sit between saints in a rich red tent, with a family kneeling in front of them. Hans Memling painted it in 1485, and the family members are shown as if they were real.
madonna-of-the-cherubim
Mary holds the baby Jesus against a red background of angels' heads. Andrea Mantegna painted it in about 1485, and the red, blue and gold are rich and dark.
madonna-of-the-red-cherubim
Mary holds her baby with a tender expression, and the heads of red cherubs float around them. Giovanni Bellini painted it in about 1485, and the red color makes the whole picture glow.
portrait-of-a-musician

A young man with curly hair holds a piece of music and looks over his shoulder as though he has been interrupted. Leonardo da Vinci painted it in about 1485, and this is the only portrait of a man by Leonardo that we know of.
the-birth-of-venus-botticelli

The goddess Venus stands on a giant scallop shell, blown by the winds to the shore, where a woman waits to cover her with a cloak. Sandro Botticelli painted it in about 1485, and it is one of the most famous pictures in the world. Venus is shown without clothes, as a goddess of love.
venus-and-mars

Mars, the god of war, sleeps deeply while Venus watches him, and little satyrs play with his armor and blow a shell in his ear. Sandro Botticelli painted it in about 1485, and the lesson is that love is stronger than war.
alzano-madonna
Mary holds the baby Jesus, in front of a stone wall and a hanging cloth, with a sweet, serious face. Giovanni Bellini painted it in about 1486.
the-annunciation-with-saint-emidius
The angel Gabriel arrives in a busy Italian town, and a small beam of light shoots into Mary's room. Carlo Crivelli painted it in 1486, and the painting is crammed with rugs, peacocks and fruit.
the-vision-of-saint-bernard
Mary appears to a monk at his desk, and angels hold the rocks of a cave around her. Filippino Lippi painted it in 1486, and the little donor portrait hides in a corner.
benedetto-portinari-s-triptych

A man kneels in prayer next to a saint, in these panels showing a family at prayer. Hans Memling painted it in 1487, and it is an example of how artists painted the people who paid for their pictures.
christ-at-the-column
A half-length Christ stands with a rope around his neck, beside a column in a dark room. Donato Bramante painted it in 1487, and he later became the architect of Saint Peter's Basilica.
diptych-of-maarten-van-nieuwenhove
A young man kneels on one panel, and on the other Mary holds the baby Jesus, offering him an apple. Hans Memling painted it in 1487, and in the round mirror behind Mary you can see the whole room.
madonna-and-child-enthroned-with-saints-and-angels

Mary sits on a throne with the baby Jesus, and saints stand beside her under a high arch while angels play music. Giovanni Bellini painted this altarpiece in 1487, and the music from the angels at her feet is lovely.
madonna-and-child-with-two-angels-saint-rose-and-saint-

Mary and the baby Jesus sit on a terrace between two angels and two saints, with a bright green countryside in the back. Pietro Perugino painted it in 1487, and the soft sky and trees are typical of him.
madonna-of-the-pomegranate
Mary holds the baby Jesus, who holds a pomegranate, and angels wrap them in a circle in this big round picture. Sandro Botticelli painted it in 1487, and the round shape is called a tondo.
the-torment-of-saint-anthony

A group of strange, scaly demons drag Saint Anthony through the air by his hair and hit him. It's attributed to the young Michelangelo, painted in about 1487 when he was about 12, and it was copied from an engraving by Martin Schongauer.
triumph-of-the-virtues
The goddess Minerva chases vices out of a garden, a bunch of strange creatures, half man and half animal, who are fleeing. Andrea Mantegna painted it in 1487 for the study of a princess.
christ-as-the-suffering-redeemer
Christ sits on the edge of his tomb with angels around him, showing his wounds and looking at us. Andrea Mantegna painted this in 1488, and it is a quiet, sorrowful image for people to meditate on.
cestello-annunciation

The angel Gabriel arrives, bowing very low, and Mary leans away in surprise, in a room that opens onto a garden. Sandro Botticelli painted it in 1489, and the sweeping lines make the figures seem to dance.
christ-with-singing-and-music-making-angels
Angels sing and play the harp, the lute, the organ and the trumpet, and some are shown reading music. Hans Memling painted these panels in 1489, and the details of the instruments are exactly right.
st-john-on-patmos

Saint John sits on a rocky island, writing his book of visions, while an angel shows him a scene of Mary in the sky. Hieronymus Bosch painted it in 1489, and on the back is a picture of the life of Christ.
an-old-man-and-his-grandson

A little boy looks up lovingly at his grandfather, whose nose is lumpy with bumps. Domenico Ghirlandaio painted it in about 1490, and he didn't hide the old man's skin condition, which makes it feel honest and warm.
ecce-homo-bosch

Christ stands with a crown of thorns before a shouting crowd, and a lot of people lean in with gleaming faces. Hieronymus Bosch painted it in about 1490, and the crowd's wild faces are painted in a spooky, cartoon-like way.
holy-allegory

Mary sits on a platform in a garden while saints stand around her, and a lake with distant hills shines beyond. Giovanni Bellini painted this puzzling picture in about 1490, and no one is sure exactly what the story is.
lady-with-an-ermine-vinci

A young woman cradles a white, stoat-like animal called an ermine in her arm, and both of them turn to look at something off to the side. Leonardo da Vinci painted Cecilia Gallerani in about 1490, and the animal was a symbol of purity and also a pun on her name.
madonna-della-candeletta
Mary holds the baby Jesus, with a candle on a ledge, in front of a rich green cloth. Carlo Crivelli painted it in about 1490, and he included his fruit and flies.
madonna-litta
Mary nurses the baby Jesus in front of two small windows, and he turns his head to look at us. This painting is attributed to Leonardo da Vinci, from about 1490,.
nativity-at-night

The baby Jesus glows with light on the ground in a night scene, and angels stand around him. Geertgen tot Sint Jans painted it in about 1490, and it is one of the first pictures to show a scene lit mainly by firelight.
